# Sirach Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_007_page_001.jpg

---

**7:1** Do no evil, and evil will never befall you.

**7:2** Depart from wrong, and it will turn away from you.

**7:3** Do not sow in the furrows of injustice, lest you harvest it sevenfold.

**7:4** Do not seek from the Lord preeminence, nor from the king a seat of honor.

**7:5** Do not justify yourself before the Lord, and do not try to appear wise before the king.

**7:6** Do not seek to become a judge, unless you have the strength to break down iniquity, for you may be partial to a powerful man and thereby put a stumbling block in the way of your integrity.

**7:7** Do not sin against the assembled city and do not cast yourself down in the popular assembly.

**7:8** Do not repeat yourself in your words, and do not let yourself be impelled to double talk.

**7:9** Do not say, "He will consider the multitude of my gifts, and when I make an offering to the Most High God, he will accept it."

**7:10** Do not be faint of heart in your prayer, and do not neglect to give alms.

**7:11** Do not ridicule a man who is in bitterness of soul, for there is one who humbles and exalts.

**7:12** Do not plot evil against your brother, nor against any friend or neighbor.

**7:13** Refuse to tell any kind of lie, for it is a habit that brings no good.

**7:14** Do not babble in the assembly of the elders, and do not repeat yourself in your prayer.

**7:15** Do not hate laborious work, and the farming that was created by the Most High.

**7:16** Do not reckon yourself among the crowd of sinners — remember that wrath will not delay.

**7:17** Humble yourself greatly, for the punishment of the ungodly is fire and worms.

**7:18** Do not exchange a friend for money, nor a dear brother for the gold of Ophir.

**7:19** Do not dismiss a wife who is sensible and good-natured, for her worth is above gold.

**7:20** Do not mistreat a servant who works faithfully, nor a hired laborer who gives himself to you.

**7:21** Let a wise servant be dear to you as yourself; do not withhold freedom from him.

**7:22** If you have cattle, look after them; if they are profitable to you, keep them.

**7:23** If you have children, discipline them, and bend their necks from their youth.

**7:24** If you have daughters, keep their bodies, and do not show too lenient a face toward them.

**7:25** Give a daughter in marriage, and you have finished a great task; but give her to a man of understanding.

**7:26** If you have a wife, do not reject her; but do not trust yourself to one whom you hate.

**7:27** Honor your father with your whole heart, and do not forget the birth pangs of your mother.

**7:28** Remember that through your parents you were born; and what can you give back to them that equals what they have given to you?

**7:29** Fear the Lord with all your soul, and reverence his priests.

**7:30** With all your strength love him who made you, and do not forsake his ministers.

**7:31** Fear the Lord and honor the priest, and give him his portion just as it is commanded: the firstfruits, the guilt offering, the shoulder portion, the sacrifice of consecration, and the firstfruits of holy things.

**7:32** Also stretch out your hand to the poor, that your blessing may be complete.

**7:33** Give graciously to all the living, and withhold not kindness from the dead.

**7:34** Do not fail those who weep, and mourn with those who mourn.

**7:35** Do not hesitate to visit the sick, for you will be loved for such things.

**7:36** In all you do, remember your end, and you will never sin.

---

*Translator's Note: Hebrew (Cairo Genizah MS A) is well preserved for this chapter. v.19 is notable — Ben Sira explicitly values an intelligent wife. v.36 "remember your end" (Greek mnēmoneue ta eschata sou) is the chapter's climax — a memento mori that grounds all the foregoing practical advice.*
